items.title: Live: Trump says senior Iranian officials killed as strikes intensify on Tehran
items.description: The United States and Israel are continuing to launch strikes at Iran as Tehran becomes increasingly isolated after attacking neighbouring countries. Follow live.

items.title: What you need to know about Iran today, with Laura Tingle
items.description: The ABC's global affairs editor, Laura Tingle, is in Dubai and will bring daily updates from the Middle East war.

items.title: Drones force US to close Gulf embassies as Trump rebukes Starmer
items.description: The US president says Iran's navy, air force and air detection systems have been "knocked out", as Israeli and US forces keep pounding targets across the country.

items.title: Marine traffic 'down to zero' due to Middle East conflict
items.description: The Strait of Hormuz normally has 50 ships moving over 100 metres, but today there are virtually zero.

items.title: Trump's Operation Epic Fury could turn out to be an epic failure
items.description: What is the White House's justification for authorising US military strikes on Iran? Right now, the answer changes every day.

items.title: Live: Taylor wants to end 'apology tour' after Liberal election review leaks
items.description: The opposition leader wants the party to move on from its "apology tour" after a review into the Liberal election loss was leaked. Follow live.

items.title: Stars are disappearing before our eyes — and something in us is shifting
items.description: For most of human history, the night sky has been a shared inheritance, a source of wonder. Now, more than a billion children see barely any stars in the night sky above their homes. So what does that mean for humanity?

items.title: Breaking: Australia's economy growing at fastest rate in almost three years
items.description: Australia's economy is growing at annual rate of 2.6 per cent, which is much stronger than forecast.

items.title: Schoolgirl becomes fourth Australian to die on Japan holiday this year
items.description: Eight-year-old Chloe Jeffries died after a snowmobile she and her mother were riding flipped, trapping her underneath it.

items.title: Kyle and Jackie O remained steadfast through scandals but the writing was on the wall
items.description: Jackie "O" Henderson has given notice saying she can no longer work with Kyle Sandilands, bringing an end to the Kyle and Jackie O Show.

items.title: Australian-made AI detects breast cancer risk previously missed
items.description: A new Australian artificial intelligence tool could transform breast cancer screening by offering a more personalised and accurate way to identify risk.

items.title: Packer's $150,000 donation to Advance a 'worrying' sign for Liberals
items.description: Liberals say billionaire James Packer's first political donation in 12 years to a conservative lobby group should be a cause for concern, saying the rise of Advance could push the party further from the mainstream.

items.title: Dynamic pricing could be coming to your local supermarket
items.description: Paper price labels are being ditched for digital ones as online-style "dynamic pricing" comes to shelves in shopping centres.

items.title: Live: Australian share market tumbles as economic growth picks up
items.description: It looks to be another ugly day on the markets as worries about a drawn-out Middle East war, surging oil prices and potentially higher inflation are fresh on investors' minds. Follow live.

items.title: Last blood moon for almost three years stuns stargazers
items.description: Australians looking to the sky on Tuesday night saw the Moon turn a reddish-orange hue, in the last total lunar eclipse until 2029.

items.title: Travel quiz: Take a trip around the world with this week's quiz
items.description: Who designed the Louvre's pyramid? And where does pastizzi come from?

items.title: Kids born during drought get to jump in puddles for the first time
items.description: Most of us have memories of jumping in big rain puddles, or making mud pies growing up, but for many regional and rural kids in SA last weekend's rain event was the first time they had popped their gumboots on.

items.title: Event planners of Barunga Festival 'blindsided' by management change
items.description: The major annual festival of Indigenous art, culture, sport and music will be run by new organisers this year, with previous event planner Sprout saying it was "blindsided" by the change in direction.

items.title: NDIS loses case with 'extremely significant' implications for plans
items.description: The agency running the NDIS has lost a legal case experts say could have significant implications for how future funding decisions are made.

items.title: Father of teenage Georgia school shooter found guilty of murder
items.description: A man who gave his teenage son the gun he is accused of using to kill two students and two teachers at a high school in the US state of Georgia has been convicted of second-degree murder.

items.title: Disabled man evicted from public housing after brother's death
items.description: A Broome man is kicked out of the public housing he has lived in for more than a decade after discovering he was not on the lease.

items.title: Ciconte's quest to become next female F1 driver moves to Japan series
items.description: Driven to reach the highest heights in motorsport, Australian teenager Joanne Ciconte sets her sights on racing in Japan.

items.title: 'An act of resistance': Iran's footballers stay silent for national anthem at Asian Cup game
items.description: As war spreads across the Middle East, Iran's women footballers are playing on at the Women's Asian Cup, having already faced a challenging road to make it to Australia.

items.title: 'Appalling' Darwin Port plans criticised by treasurer who leased it
items.description: Former NT treasurer Dave Tollner describes the federal government's plans to take back the 99-year lease of Darwin Port as "an appalling waste of money".

items.title: Liquidators find sports centre company owes creditors on top of $61m tax debt
items.description: Employees and suppliers are among 140 secured and unsecured creditors of Queensland Indoor Arenas, run by Colin and Ashlee Kinnest with centres in Bundaberg, Brisbane and Logan.
